When Ibn az-Zubair took the caliphate, Ibn Abbas refused to fight in Mecca, praised his lineage and piety, yet felt rebuffed and preferred his own cousins as rulers.
The Prophet shared something among four men to win their hearts; a man accused him of injustice, and he said the man's offspring would produce people who renounce the religion.
When alms were ordered, companions worked as porters to have something to give; hypocrites mocked small and large gifts alike, and a verse came about those who criticise voluntary givers.
The Prophet gave his shirt and offered the funeral prayer for Abdullah bin Ubai despite Umar's objection, then a verse forbade praying for any of them who dies.
Ka'b bin Malik, who stayed behind from Tabuk, said that after Islam no blessing was greater than speaking the truth to the Prophet instead of lying like others.
In a dream the Prophet saw people half handsome and half ugly, who had mixed good and bad deeds, made wholly handsome in a river, for Allah forgave them.
As Abu Talib lay dying the Prophet urged him to declare Allah's oneness and promised to seek forgiveness for him, till a verse forbade seeking forgiveness for pagans, even kin.
Ka'b bin Malik told how he and two others who stayed behind from Tabuk were shunned until Allah forgave them, and how telling the truth saved him.
After Yamama, Abu Bakr, urged by Umar, had Zaid bin Thabit collect the Quran from writings and memories, finding two verses of At-Tauba only with Khuza'ima.
Finding the Jews of Medina fasting Ashura for Moses' victory over Pharaoh, the Prophet said Muslims have more right to it and told them to fast.
Ibn Abbas said 'they fold up their breasts' concerned people too shy to relieve themselves or have relations with their wives in the open under the sky.
Allah says, spend and I will spend on you; His Hand is full and unreduced by spending since creation, His Throne was over the water, and He holds the balance.
Allah will screen the believer, make him confess his sins and forgive what He concealed in the world, while the disbelievers will be exposed before witnesses.
Allah gives respite to the oppressor, but when He seizes him He never lets him go, as the verse on seizing wrongdoing towns says.
A man who kissed a woman told the Prophet, and the verse came that prayer and good deeds remove evil deeds, which the Prophet said is for all his followers.
Joseph is the honourable son of honourable prophets back to Abraham; asked who is most honourable, the Prophet named the pious, Joseph, then those best before Islam who understand it.
During the slander against her Aisha likened herself to Joseph's father, saying patience is most fitting, until Allah revealed her innocence.
Ibn Masud recited 'Haita laka' and said they recite it as they were taught it.
When Quraysh delayed embracing Islam the Prophet prayed for seven famine years like Joseph's; they ate bones and saw smoke between them and the sky, as the verses describe.
The Prophet asked mercy for Lot, said he would have answered the call after an imprisonment as long as Joseph's, and that we have more right to doubt than Abraham.
Aisha explained that the messengers despaired of their disbelieving people and thought their followers called them liars, never suspecting that Allah had betrayed them.
The keys of the Unseen are five, known only to Allah: what tomorrow brings, what is in the wombs, the rain, the place of death and the Hour.
The Prophet asked about a tree like a Muslim whose leaves never fall; Ibn Umar thought of the date palm but kept quiet, and Umar wished he had spoken.
Questioned in his grave, the Muslim testifies that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger, the firm word of the verse.
Ibn Abbas said those who changed Allah's favour into disbelief were the disbelieving pagans of Mecca.
When Allah decrees a matter the angels beat their wings in obedience; eavesdropping devils pass snatches down, unless a flame strikes, to a sorcerer who adds a hundred lies.
On the way to Tabuk the Prophet told his companions to enter the dwellings of Al-Hijr's people only weeping, lest they suffer what struck them.
The Prophet named Al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses, the greatest sura and the substance of the Quran, after asking Abu Sa'id why he had not answered his call.
Ibn Abbas said those who split the Scripture into parts, believing some and disbelieving the rest, are the Jews and Christians.
The Prophet sought refuge with Allah from miserliness, laziness, old age, the punishment of the grave, the Dajjal's affliction and the afflictions of life and death.
Ibn Masud said the suras Bani Israel, Al-Kahf and Maryam are among his first old treasures.
On the night journey the Prophet chose milk over wine, and when Quraysh disbelieved him Allah displayed Bait-ul-Maqdis before him so he could describe it.
Ibn Masud said that before Islam, when a tribe grew numerous, people said 'amira' of it.
On Resurrection Day people in distress will ask Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus to intercede, each declining, until Muhammad prostrates beneath the Throne and his intercession is accepted.
Reciting the Psalms was made so easy for David that he finished before his mount was saddled.
Ibn Masud said the verse on those called upon who seek access to their Lord concerns jinn worshipped by some people, who became Muslims while their worshippers kept their religion.
Ibn Abbas said the vision in the verse was an actual sight shown to the Prophet on his night journey, and the cursed tree is the tree of Zaqqum.
Congregational prayer is twenty-five times better than praying alone, and the angels of night and day gather at Fajr, whose recitation the verse calls witnessed.
On Resurrection Day nations will seek intercession until it is given to Muhammad at the praised station; whoever asks this for him after the adhan will receive his intercession.
Entering Mecca in the year of the Conquest, the Prophet struck the 360 idols around the Ka'bah with a stick, reciting that truth has come and falsehood has vanished.
